title: Alonzo Church, Lambda Calculus, and the Formal Idea of a Function
explainer: The idea of a function that takes an input and hands back an output — and a recursive function defined in terms of a smaller call to itself — is directly descended from lambda calculus, a formal system the logician Alonzo Church introduced in the 1930s to study what 'computable' even means. Church built lambda calculus using nothing but function definition and function application, and it turned out to be exactly as powerful as Alan Turing's Turing machine. That result, the Church–Turing thesis, still underlies what computer scientists mean when they say a problem is or isn't solvable by a program.
